ranking.name: Scuffed Cement
ranking.assessment: Closest quiet, dry taupe cement coating; no masonry courses or obvious panel grid. It preserves the existing rocky relief without strong fake crack shapes. Its fine wear is subtle at visitor distance and can look too plain; compare both feature sizes rather than assuming 2× wins.

ranking.name: Concrete Wall 008
ranking.assessment: The lighter muted grey coating is readable on the entrance and closer to the grey/off-white reference family. It has source construction seams and formwork marks visible on inspection, so it is a useful alternative, not an unqualified recommendation. The added 2× comparison makes that pattern risk explicit.

ranking.name: Cracked Concrete Wall
ranking.assessment: Strongest visibly weathered/chalky option, with genuine scan detail and peeling mineral-like patches. The 2× version reduces small busy repetition, but its light albedo and high-contrast damage can be too pale/blotchy compared with the subdued reference. Review as the more weathered alternative.

ranking.name: Chipped Concrete
ranking.assessment: Good neutral grey tone and clear dry pitting. Actual close views reveal a regular stippled/tooling pattern that can resemble an artificial finish, especially when enlarged. Do not confuse scan detail with a convincing final cave coating.

ranking.name: Concrete Wall 006
ranking.assessment: Authentic worn cement with small pits and scratches, but darker than the desired readable coating in this scene. Recurring construction joints/formwork details are a further risk. Both feature sizes are included; it is weaker at the landing than its catalog/source appearance suggests.

ranking.name: Worn Plaster Wall
ranking.assessment: Recognisable damaged plaster but large repeated peeled patches read as camouflage-like spotting on the cave, and the source has a recurring construction joint. Less coherent than the references at normal viewing distance.

ranking.name: Plaster Stone Wall 02
ranking.assessment: Dusty plaster palette is relevant, but exposed stone courses imply arranged masonry. It does not preserve the desired unstructured cement-covered-rock appearance.

ranking.name: Plastered Stone Wall
ranking.assessment: Weathered scan with subdued variation, but nearly black under the unchanged scene lighting. Both sizes demonstrate that enlarging features cannot solve low material readability; not a recommended final coating.

ranking.name: Quarry Wall — earlier-study control
ranking.assessment: Retains coarse geological grain and a dark mineral response, but reads as quarry rock rather than aged canal cement. Useful for comparison with earlier work; not a dried-canal finalist.

ranking.name: Rock Embedded Concrete Wall
ranking.assessment: Strong orange/brown aggregate and arranged stone forms read as masonry or a repeated stone skin. It conflicts with the restrained grey-beige coating target despite being a valid licensed scan.

recommendation: Review Scuffed Cement and Concrete Wall 008 first as contrasting subdued and lighter cement options. Cracked Concrete Wall at larger features is the optional strongly weathered alternative. Every recommendation has the limitations above; none is selected, visually approved or promoted. No candidate exactly reproduces the photographs on this locked organic mesh under the existing dark lighting.
